clue.text: Like the Ancient Mariner's ship, tide- and weather-battered

indicators.note: something battered has been knocked out of shape, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coleridge's becalmed ship, pictured as knocked about by tide and storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' rearranges all fourteen letters of TIDE AND WEATHER. The surface is unfair to the poem: the ship was stuck motionless, which is the point of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Coleridge's poem the ship lies becalmed and helpless, the idiom for something stalled with no prospect of moving.

clue.text: Girl's staidness cracked: maybe a flare-up

indicators.note: a thing that has cracked has broken apart, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prim girl's composure finally breaks, and she has an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' rearranges the letters of GIRLS STAIDNESS. 'flare-up' looks like a temper tantrum, but the hyphenated word is a literal flare sent up.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare fired into the sky is one example of a call for help from a ship or stranded party.

clue.text: Fish (salmon) short of some oxygen, caught by a fleet out of area

indicators.note: something caught by another is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other
out of means without, so the letter for area is taken away

parts.note: a fleet of warships is a navy

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so one letter is removed from the salmon

parts.note: the coho is a species of Pacific salmon
O is the symbol for oxygen; one of the two Os is dropped

explanation.surface: A salmon, deprived of oxygen, is caught by a fishing fleet away from its usual ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets round 'salmon' make it look like an aside on the fish; it is wordplay, while 'Fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The anchovy is a small, oily sea fish, a familiar salted ingredient on pizzas.

clue.text: There's no way to break sinful fraud

indicators.note: to break something is to split it open, so other letters are set inside the word

parts.note: sinful means impure
O, the figure nought, stands for no or nothing
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A moralist declares that nothing can disrupt a wicked swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' is only a link; 'no way' splits into two pieces, nought and street.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposture is a deception carried out by pretending to be someone else, a kind of swindle.

clue.text: In football move, run faster to leave United floundering

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
to leave is to depart, so this letter goes out of the fodder

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A player is told to sprint faster in order to escape struggling Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes U out of RUN FASTER, and 'floundering' rearranges the remaining RNFASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A transfer is a player's sale from one club to another, the commonest kind of change of club in soccer.

clue.text: Approval as European joins up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so it runs backwards

parts.note: joins means meets, as roads meet

explanation.surface: A European country signs up to an alliance and gets the nod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' works because this is a down clue, read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard or respect, the favourable opinion behind approval.

clue.text: Took part, having excellent day — about time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so these letters go round the letter for time

parts.note: ace means excellent

explanation.surface: Someone joined in and had a brilliant day, more or less on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ACE and D round T.
explanation.definitionFit: To take part in a play is to have acted a role in it, playing a character.

clue.text: More than usually insulting, artist chucked press out

indicators.note: chucked means thrown out, so these letters are dropped from the phrase

parts.note: more than usually insulting is extra rude
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter, being unusually offensive, was thrown out by the reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucked' removes RA from EXTRA RUDE. 'press' looks like journalists, but it is a verb in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrude is to force material through an opening to shape it, as with pasta or plastic.

clue.text: After fruit drink, book entertains those who like to wallow

parts.note: a hip is the fruit of the rose
pop is a fizzy soft drink
OT, the Old Testament, is a book of the Bible
entertains means amuses

explanation.surface: After a fruity drink, a book keeps idlers who enjoy lounging amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those who like to wallow' sounds like idle humans, but it is the mud-loving animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippos spend their days half-submerged in rivers and mud pools, keeping their skin cool and moist.

clue.text: Refuse to accept bad copy? Yes man!

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the jumbled letters go inside

parts.note: shan't is a curt refusal, shall not

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters of copy are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor declines to take a poor piece of writing, and someone agrees obsequiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like rubbish; it is a verb, giving a curt refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant flatters the powerful by agreeing with everything they say, the classic toady.

clue.text: African mentioning child's foot

indicators.note: mentioning means saying out loud, so the answer sounds like the word given

parts.note: tootsie is a childish word for a foot

explanation.surface: An African talks about a youngster's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioning' signals a word that sounds like TOOTSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Criminals being executed? They start off being first rankers

definitions.text: They start off being first rankers

indicators.note: executing someone takes off their head, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: crooks are criminals

explanation.surface: Criminals are put to death, while the first in line take their places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being executed' beheads CROOKS. 'first rankers' sounds military; it means pieces on a chessboard's back row.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess both castles begin the game in the corners of the player's first rank.

clue.text: One enforcing a go-slow emptied water barrel into reservoir

indicators.note: into means going inside, so these letters are put within the reservoir

parts.note: a sump is a reservoir or pit where liquid collects
to pee is to pass water, to urinate
D is short for drained, emptied, as in the abbreviation for dried or deceased
B is an abbreviation for barrel, as in oil output given in b/d

explanation.surface: A slowdown is staged by draining a water barrel into a reservoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go-slow' suggests a strike; here it is traffic slowing down.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised ridge across a road forces drivers to slow down, a physical traffic-calming measure.

clue.text: Character of composition briefly requires pens

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the character of a piece of writing is its style
requires means uses, as a task uses or needs resources

explanation.surface: An essay's style, put simply, needs writing instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops only the last letter, the usual sense of curtailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is a pointed writing implement, as used on wax tablets or touchscreens.

clue.text: PC in court opened eyes?

parts.note: politically correct, now often called woke
someone up before the magistrate is in court

explanation.surface: A police constable in a courtroom has his eyes opened.
explanation.walkthrough: PC wants to be police constable; it is politically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening your eyes after sleep is what it means to rise from slumber, the literal sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Slip-up on particular area in speech

parts.note: over means on, as in a cover over or on something

indicators.note: in speech means spoken out loud, so the second part sounds like the word given

parts.note: a site is a particular area or location

explanation.surface: A speaker makes a mistake about a specific region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' signals SIGHT, sounding like SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a mistake made through failing to notice something, an error or lapse.

clue.text: Sweet I stuff into ill-fitting suit

indicators.note: into means going inside, so these letters are put within the rearranged ones
an ill-fitting garment is out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to stuff is to ram, to cram in

explanation.surface: Someone cramming themselves into a suit that is too small.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged suit is TISU; the inserted letters go after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge layered with mascarpone cream.

clue.text: Private meal changed in second

indicators.note: the meal is altered at its second letter, so that letter is swapped for another

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A soldier's meal was altered in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed in second' swaps SUPPER's second letter U for A. 'Private' looks like an adjective, but it is the soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Engineers a sapper is the lowest rank, the equivalent of a private soldier.

clue.text: Overcome impudence that holds state up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, so the whole is reversed
holds means contains, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: lip is cheek or impudence
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Cheek that props up a nation wins the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' makes LIAVERP before 'up', a down-clue reversal, turns the whole thing round.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win through against opposition, triumphing over it.

clue.text: Large amount put on paper in set period

indicators.note: in an across clue put on means added after, so the amount follows the paper

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper
a lot is a large amount

explanation.surface: Lots written on paper in a fixed stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TIMES is a British national newspaper, a crossword favourite for paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A time slot is an allotted interval in a schedule, such as for a broadcast.

clue.text: Before a long time, lake lost because of this?

definitions.text: Before a long time, lake lost because of this?

indicators.note: before means coming first, so the jumbled letters precede the next piece
lost means astray, so the letters of lake are rearranged

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A lake drains away over the years, and the question is what caused it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges the lake into LEAK. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a slow escape of water empties a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is the gradual escape of liquid through a hole, which could drain a lake over time.

clue.text: Being extravagant with jewellery all over uniform

indicators.note: all over means covering on every side, so these letters surround the other

parts.note: bling is flashy jewellery
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone showing off with gold chains covering a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' puts BLING round U. To blue money is a British slang spelling of blow, to squander.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue money is British slang for spending it recklessly, squandering it.

clue.text: A month back, foul up badly in it? That's irregular

indicators.note: in means going inside, so these letters are placed within the reversed month
back means going the wrong way, so the month is written backwards

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August, a month
to foul up is to err, to make a mistake
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Things went seriously wrong a month ago, and that was unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives GUA, and 'it' points to that reversed month. 'irregular' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregular is a soldier outside a regular army, which is what a guerrilla fighter is.

clue.text: Sage from Dublin I dropped completely

indicators.note: in a down clue a letter dropped completely falls all the way to the bottom

parts.note: Dublin is the Irish capital, so from Dublin means Irish

explanation.surface: A wise man from Ireland's capital says he gave up totally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped completely' moves the first I of IRISH to the end of the word, its bottom in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism a rishi is an inspired holy seer, a sage to whom the Vedas were revealed.

clue.text: A lot of insects took to the water to cross river

indicators.note: to cross is to span, so these letters straddle the letter for river

parts.note: to take to the water is to swim, so swam

explanation.surface: A cloud of insects managed to swim across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cross' puts SWAM round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large moving mass of insects, especially bees leaving a hive.

clue.text: Notice a lady is president twice

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
Ms is a title for a woman

explanation.surface: An observer remarks that a woman holds the top office for a second term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb, but it is an ad. 'twice' because two US presidents had this surname, John Adams and his son.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams, father and son, were the second and sixth US presidents.

clue.text: Fish product is ready to drink?

parts.note: a drink poured in a glass is ready to drink

explanation.surface: A query on whether a fish-based item can be drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: IS is taken as written, followed by IN GLASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a gelatin made from fish swim bladders, used to clear beer and wine.

clue.text: Perhaps church support aeronautics, though something hairy

parts.note: aeronautics is the science of flying
but means though, however
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A cathedral needs an aviation expert, though the engineering looks risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something hairy' sounds like dangerous, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying buttress is an arched prop bracing the walls of Gothic cathedrals, an example of architectural support.
